Learning Path

Multithreading in C++: from theory to a working state machine

Level: intermediate (assumes basic C++) 21 lessons 22 lessons

A pragmatic learning path for those who already know the basics of C++ but have never had to run multiple threads within the same process without shooting themselves in the foot. We start with the bare minimum theory — what a thread really is and what can go wrong — and then move on to more sophisticated concepts. Each module ends with a project where you will put into practice what you have just learned.

The lessons should be completed in order: each project builds upon the concepts introduced in the theory immediately preceding it.

You can find all the source code for the course in this repository.

Start the course

What you'll learn, module by module

Module 0 — Fundamentals

01 What a thread really is (and why you suddenly need to know) Theory 02 When shared memory bites: race conditions, data races, and Qt's single thread Theory 03 Two demonstrations, not two stories: the race condition and the freeze built with your own hands Project

Module 1 — QThread: the Two Models and Qt's Event Loop Architecture

04 QThread is not the thread: it's a remote control (and why subclassing it is misleading) Theory 05 Two event loops talking safely: queued connections and the lifecycle of a worker thread Theory 06 Project: curing the freeze for real, by moving the computation to a worker thread Project

Module 2 — Synchronization: Mutexes, Wait Conditions, Semaphores, and Classic Problems

07 The critical section, formalized: QMutex, QMutexLocker, and QReadWriteLock Theory 08 Waiting for an event, not a lock: QWaitCondition, QSemaphore, and how to shoot yourself in the foot Theory 09 The Day Mars Almost Won: Pathfinder and Priority Inversion Theory 10 Project: producer, consumer, and the buffer that keeps them in balance Project

Module 3 — QtConcurrent and Future/Promise model

11 QtConcurrent::run, mapped/filtered/reduced, and the QThreadPool behind the scenes Theory 12 QFuture, QFutureWatcher, and the question vibe coding always skips Theory 13 Project: batch image processing with QtConcurrent::mapped and QFutureWatcher Project

Module 4 — Safe Communication Between Threads: Qt Connections and Cooperative Cancellation

14 The four Qt::ConnectionType values: what really happens when you write connect() Theory 15 QMetaObject::invokeMethod and cooperative cancellation: calling and stopping a thread without risk Theory 16 Project: a worker's complete life cycle — start, pause, resume, stop Project

Module 5 — Advanced Patterns: Custom Thread Pools, Atomics, and the Hidden Cost of Cache

17 QRunnable and QThreadPool: a pool of tasks, not a thread per job Theory 18 std::atomic, the C++ memory model, and the performance bug you can't see in the code Theory 19 Project: benchmarking mutex vs atomic, false sharing, and verification with ThreadSanitizer Project

Module 6 — Capstone Project: Near-Real-Time Vision Pipeline

20 Capstone: architecture of a vision pipeline — capture and bounded buffer Theory 21 Capstone: persistent processing pool and full cooperative cancellation Theory 22 Capstone Project: near real-time frame processing pipeline Project
